fichas.title: Squash courts
fichas.summary: Squash courts are described as having massive walls with special plastered surfaces, precast concrete elements, prefabricated panelled timber-framed roofs and potentially collapsible seating. A glass back wall is advantageous for spectators. The floor should be slightly springy, light-coloured wood with good slip resistance; floorboards run parallel to the side walls. Walls are flat white special plaster, with a metal or metal-clad strip (the tin) at the foot of the front wall.

fichas.title: Table tennis halls and playing area
fichas.summary: Championship-level table tennis is played in halls. The table surface is horizontal, matt green and marked with white border lines. The playing box is formed by canvas screens; spectators are beyond the screen. For outdoor tables, fibre-cement board is specified.

fichas.title: Billiards rooms and table sizes
fichas.summary: Billiards rooms are preferably on the first floor or in a well-lit basement. The text gives spacing guidance for billiards tables, recommends extra space at waiter and spectator sides, and calls for space for chairs, tables, food and drink. It also describes cue-rack mounting and even lighting over the playing area. Table sizes are tabulated by class I–VI.
